summary.plain: DarkSide-LowMass is a proposed 1.5-tonne liquid argon detector designed to detect dark matter lighter than about 10 GeV through the faint electric charge it would free in the argon. It is a project of the Global Argon Dark Matter Collaboration; the primary plan is to install it at SNOLAB in Canada.
summary.technical: Conceptual design (Phys. Rev. D 107, 112006): dual-phase LAr TPC in an acrylic vessel viewed by two photosensor arrays, inside a bath of underground argon (veto) in a cryostat in a water tank, optimised for an electron-counting (ionisation-only) analysis with 2 or 4 electron thresholds; projected sensitivity to GeV-scale dark matter down to the solar-neutrino floor and to 10 MeV/c^2 with the Migdal effect or electron scattering. The 2025 SNOLAB report gives 1.5 t (1 t fiducial) and a primary plan to place the inner detector in the DEAP-3600 water tank; the 2022 paper left the site open ('LNGS or a lab comparably far from Aria'). No approval or funding decision was found.
